Friday Focus Tip #42: The Client Enquiry Process That Qualifies

Not every enquiry deserves a yes.

A weak enquiry process means you waste time quoting jobs that won't work, dealing with difficult clients, or chasing people who never commit.

Here's how to qualify properly:

• Ask about their cleaning needs upfront
• Find out their budget expectations
• Understand their timeline
• Gauge if they value quality or just price
• Check if they fit your service area
• Listen for red flags (unrealistic demands, constant haggling)
• Be clear about your terms and standards

A good enquiry process does two things:

1. It filters out the wrong clients early
2. It attracts the right ones by being professional and clear

The clients who book with you should feel confident they've chosen someone reliable. And you should feel confident you can deliver for them.

Friday Focus Tip #41: The Hidden Cost of Staff Turnover

High staff turnover is expensive. Really expensive.

Most cleaning business owners only count the cost of recruiting and training. But the real damage is deeper:

• Lost productivity during handover
• Mistakes made by new staff
• Clients leaving because their regular cleaner left
• Time spent managing the chaos
• Inconsistent quality damaging your reputation
• New staff needing more supervision

Here's what works:

• Pay fairly (you get what you pay for)
• Create a supportive team environment
• Offer flexibility where possible
• Recognise good work
• Provide clear training and standards
• Have a career path (even a small one)
• Deal with problem staff quickly

Keeping good people is cheaper than constantly replacing them.

Friday Focus Tip #40: The Art of Saying No

Not every enquiry is a good fit. And that's okay.

A lot of cleaning business owners say yes to everything because they're afraid of losing income. But the wrong clients cost you more than they're worth.

The wrong client might:

• Expect endless discounts
• Complain about everything
• Demand last-minute changes
• Leave bad reviews
• Pull your team's energy down
• Eat into your profit margins

Your time and your team's sanity are valuable.

So before you say yes to a new client, ask yourself:

Is this the right fit for my business? Will my team enjoy working for them? Can I deliver at my quality standard? Will they respect my pricing?

If the answer to any of those is no, it's okay to say no.

The best cleaning businesses aren't the ones that take every job. They're the ones that take the right jobs.
